chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام led us in the fajr prayer and recited al-Ḍuḥā and Alam Nashraḥ in one rakʿah. So this does not contradict what we have stated regarding the dislike of joining two surahs together, because these two surahs are one surah according to Āl Muḥammad عليهم السلام, and one should recite them together in one place and not separate between them with Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm in the obligatory prayers, and this report does not contradict that.

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as the authoritative source here
key_terms.الْقِرَانِ: joining two surahs together in one rakʿah
key_terms.بِبِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: the basmalah that should not be used to separate these two surahs in obligatory prayer

ai.seo_question: Why does reciting al-Ḍuḥā and Alam Nashraḥ together in obligatory prayer not count as combining two surahs?
ai.summary: This report concerns the recitation of Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā and Sūrat Alam Nashraḥ together in obligatory prayer. It explains that combining them does not fall under the disliked ruling of joining two separate surahs, because according to Āl Muḥammad عليهم السلام they are treated as a single surah in this context.
